judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The newsletter E-mail field in the footer, whose placeholder "E-mail" is its visible label, so the placeholder is text under 1.4.3 (11px, weight 300, needs 4.5:1). The footer stylesheet the page loads (css chunk 0d5b24039af96206, footer chunk 2245) sets .Newsletter_emailInput__XLU6p::placeholder{color:#707070} on a transparent input over the #f7f7f7 footer. The screenshot agrees: zoomed, the placeholder glyphs are drawn with subpixel (coloured-fringe) antialiasing, every channel bottoms out at exactly 0x70 and the fully covered pixels are #707070, while #707097 is one of the fringe colours (#977070, #7083b1, #707097). #707070 on #f7f7f7 is 4.62:1, above 4.5:1. claimTrue: no, the stated colour and 4.40:1 are an antialiasing artefact of the pixel sample, not the text colour. elementFails: no. captureDiffers: no, the live CSS and the capture agree. Cause: the rule had a correct screenshot and took a fringe pixel for the text colour.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: [visual context] The product image link of the Cinto De Couro Minibold card: aria-label="1" (the browser computes the name "1" from aria-label), no title or aria-describedby, and it leads to the page titled "Cinto De Couro Minibold"; claimTrue: yes. Context per the rubric: it sits in div/article containers, not in a sentence, paragraph, list item or table cell; the heading just before it in document order is the previous card's h3 "Brinco Dourado Longo Pedra Snake", which names another product. The product name that explains it is the h3 inside a separate link after the image, which is not in its context (F63; H2 would be the fix), so only that visible headline and the photo tell a sighted user where it goes. The purpose is not ambiguous to users in general. elementFails: yes. The live shelf code still sets the link's aria-label from the first image's alternateName, which is still "1" for this product; captureDiffers: no. The claim names this failure.
